canonical.title: A weekend in Le Castellet, anchored on La Table du Castellet

children.title: Day-trips and activities within 30 km of La Table du Castellet
Walking-distance lodging at or near La Table du Castellet
Special-character lodging within taxi range of La Table du Castellet

sources.title: La Table du Castellet — official restaurant page
sources.claim: La Table du Castellet at 3001 Route des Hauts du Camp, Le Castellet; 3 Michelin stars since March 2024; dinner Wed-Sat, lunch Fri-Sun.

sources.title: Hôtel & Spa du Castellet — official site
sources.claim: 5★ Relais & Châteaux, 43 rooms, 700 m² spa, on a 12-ha umbrella-pine park at 430 m; same building as La Table.

sources.title: Michelin Guide — La Table du Castellet
sources.claim: Three Michelin stars, retained in the 2026 guide; chef Fabien Ferré.

sources.title: Region tourism — Hôtel & Spa du Castellet
sources.claim: Annual closure: 1 Dec – 28 Feb 2026; voted Best Luxury Spa in Europe 2019.

sources.title: Grand Prix Hôtel — Access
sources.claim: 3★ at 3100 Route des Hauts du Camp, on Circuit Paul Ricard — about 700 m east of La Table along an unlit country road.

sources.title: TripAdvisor — Grand Prix Hôtel
sources.claim: Standard rooms $88-$241; 117 rooms; 4.3/5 from 596 reviews.

sources.title: TripAdvisor — Hôtel & Spa du Castellet
sources.claim: Standard nightly rates $303-$939; 4.6/5 from 926 reviews.

sources.title: Maison Bérard — official site
sources.claim: 4★ family-run hotel in La Cadière-d'Azur with 32 Provençal rooms across four village buildings, Riva restaurant, AromaSpa.

sources.title: Hostellerie de l'Abbaye de la Celle — official site
sources.claim: 5★ 10-room 18th-c. inn beside the Abbey of La Celle, transformed by Alain Ducasse in 1999.

sources.title: Île Rousse Thalazur Bandol — listing
sources.claim: 5★ seafront on Renécros Bay with 55 rooms + 12 suites, infinity pool of heated sea water, 100 m² thalasso area.

sources.title: Les Roches Blanches Cassis — official site
sources.claim: 1887 mansion between Cassis village and the Calanques with Cap Canaille views; Sisley Spa; 4 dining venues.

sources.title: Rome2Rio — La Celle to Le Castellet
sources.claim: 48.9 km / about 49 minutes by car — outer edge of practical late-night taxi range.

sources.title: Rome2Rio — Cassis to Le Castellet
sources.claim: 25.6 km / 21 minutes by car; taxi $70-$90.

sources.title: Rome2Rio — Bandol to Le Castellet
sources.claim: 10.3 km / about 15 minutes by car; taxi $30-$40.

sources.title: Var VTC service note
sources.claim: Le Castellet has no permanent taxi stand; pre-booking a VTC by phone is the standard pattern for evening pickups.

sources.title: Plus Beaux Villages de France — Le Castellet
sources.claim: Classified Plus Beau Village; 12th-c. church Église de la Transfiguration; perched medieval village distinct from the hotel plateau.

sources.title: Le Castellet tourisme — Pagnol filming trail
sources.claim: Marcel Pagnol filmed La Femme du Boulanger here in summer 1938; Place de l'Ormeau, Rue Droite, the Portail, Angèle's house at 6 Rue de l'Aube.

sources.title: Provence Sud Sainte-Baume — La Cadière-d'Azur
sources.claim: Perched village on the opposite cliff to Le Castellet, ~5 km away, with 360° panorama over the Bandol vineyards.

sources.title: Domaine Tempier — official site
sources.claim: Open Monday to Friday only, 9-12 and 13:30-17:30, closed weekends and public holidays — inaccessible on a pure weekend.

sources.title: Château de Pibarnon — official site
sources.claim: Cellar in La Cadière-d'Azur open Monday to Saturday by appointment; closed Sunday and public holidays.

sources.title: Domaine de la Bégude — Oenotourism
sources.claim: Experiences €15-€89 at Le Camp du Castellet including 4×4 vineyard tours and picnic lunches; online booking up to 24h ahead.

sources.title: Maison des Vins de Bandol — Le Castellet
sources.claim: Le Castellet shop Tue-Sat 10-13 / 15-19; in June, July and August a different vigneron hosts a commented tasting daily.

sources.title: Domaine Ott — Château Romassan
sources.claim: Mourvèdre-led estate in Le Castellet, modernised cellar in 2023, offers exclusive tastings of rosé, white and red.

sources.title: Bandol Tourisme — Bendor reopens 2026
sources.claim: Île de Bendor reopens 1 May 2026 under Zannier Hotels: three guesthouses (Delos, Soukana, Madrague), restaurants, building on Ricard's 1958 wine-museum legacy.

sources.title: Bendor shuttle — official schedule
sources.claim: Bendor shuttle runs 1 May - 1 Nov 2026, every 30 minutes 10:00-23:30; 7-minute crossing; online-only ticketing.

sources.title: Bandol Tourisme — Bandol wines
sources.claim: Bandol AOC dates from 1941; 3000 hours of sunshine; powerful Mourvèdre reds and pale-salmon rosés define its character.

sources.title: Sanary tourisme — Wednesday market
sources.claim: Sanary's Wednesday market runs 8am-1pm year-round along the port; 300+ vendors; voted most beautiful market in France by TF1 viewers 2018.

sources.title: Sanary tourisme — Land of exile
sources.claim: 1933-1940 Sanary hosted Thomas Mann, Lion Feuchtwanger and other German intellectuals fleeing Nazi book burnings; world capital of artistic and literary exile.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Eden Theatre, La Ciotat
sources.claim: Guinness-recognised oldest purpose-built cinema in operation; opened 1889; hosted the first paying Lumière screening in 1899; reopened 2013.

sources.title: Destination La Ciotat — Cradle of cinema
sources.claim: Louis Lumière perfected the cinematograph in La Ciotat summer 1895; first paying screening 21 March 1899 at Eden Théâtre.

sources.title: Cassis tourisme — Calanques
sources.claim: En-Vau (the most spectacular, steep white cliffs), Port-Pin (the most intimate, Aleppo pines), Port-Miou — Cassis's three signature calanques.

sources.title: Cassis tourisme — Calanques access
sources.claim: Fire-risk daily colour code in summer; on RED days the massif is closed all day; forecast updated at 18:00 for the next day, June to September.

sources.title: Parc national des Calanques — 2026 reservations
sources.claim: Free prior reservation required for Port-Miou/Port-Pin/En-Vau weekend 20-21 June, daily 27 June - 30 August, weekends 5-6 Sept and 12-13 Sept 2026.

sources.title: Region tourism — Cap Canaille
sources.claim: Cap Canaille between Cassis and La Ciotat at 399 m — highest sea cliff in Europe; D141 Route des Crêtes ridge road.

sources.title: Parc national des Calanques — Cap Canaille
sources.claim: Route des Crêtes automatically closed on red fire-risk days 1 June - 30 September; do not approach the cliff edge.

sources.title: Parc national des Calanques — Île Verte
sources.claim: Only wooded island in the Calanques National Park; shuttle from Old Port of La Ciotat April-October; 1-hour walking loop; swim at La Plageolle and Seynerolles.

sources.title: Destination La Ciotat — Île Verte shuttle
sources.claim: Aquilade shuttle, 10-min crossing; July-Aug 2026 hourly 09:00-18:00; adult return €14, child under 10 €9.

sources.title: Bandol Tourisme — Île des Embiez
sources.claim: Blue-Flag, Natura-2000-listed Paul Ricard island reachable in ~12 min from Le Brusc, with a 360°-view fort and 90% of regional Med plant species.

sources.title: Île des Embiez — Tickets
sources.claim: 12-minute ferry from Le Brusc year-round; summer service also from Sanary 6 June – 26 Sept 2026; adult day tickets €10-€21.

sources.title: Circuit Paul Ricard — Driving Experiences
sources.claim: On-circuit programmes: GTDrive supercars, Winfield Racing School Formula, EasyMonneret motorcycle training, two-seater passenger laps, karting.

sources.title: Toulon Tourisme — Mont Faron cable car
sources.claim: Mont Faron at 584 m above Toulon, reached by a cable car unique on the Mediterranean coast, with WWII Mémorial du Débarquement de Provence and Zoo du Faron at the summit.

sources.title: MPM Tourisme — Mont Faron cable car
sources.claim: Transparent floor; runs daily Feb-Nov (some Mondays in Feb/Mar closed); Pass Téléphérique/Fauverie €18 adult / €13 child.

sources.title: Bateliers de la Côte d'Azur — Rade de Toulon tour
sources.claim: 1-hour guided harbour tour daily 7 Feb - 1 Nov 2026; adult €15.50, child (4-10) €11; views of the Charles de Gaulle aircraft carrier and stealth frigates.

sources.title: Toulon — Marché du Cours Lafayette
sources.claim: Provençal market ~1 km long every morning except Monday 07:30-12:30 on Cours Lafayette.

sources.title: Region tourism — Plage des Lecques
sources.claim: 2-km family sand beach at Saint-Cyr-sur-Mer, lined by the Pink Promenade.

sources.title: Plages.tv — Renécros, Bandol
sources.claim: Sheltered bay of rare fine white sand with a gentle slope, lifeguard, paddle boats, snack bars — Bandol's best family beach.

sources.title: Aqualand Saint-Cyr-sur-Mer
sources.claim: 2026 season Sat 20 June - Sun 6 September; located 900 m from Plage des Lecques.

sources.title: OK Corral — visitor info
sources.claim: Largest amusement park in southern France, 4 km from Circuit Paul Ricard at Cuges-les-Pins; 2026 season 4 April - 1 November.

sources.title: Visit Var — Notre-Dame du Beausset-Vieux
sources.claim: 12th-c. Romano-Provençal chapel at 383 m, listed national monument since 1970; remarkable panorama over the perched villages and Bandol vineyards.

sources.title: Region tourism — Grotte Sainte-Marie-Madeleine
sources.claim: About a 45-minute climb above the Hôtellerie via stations of the Crucifixion; cave temperature a constant 13°C.

sources.title: ViaMichelin — Toulon to Le Castellet
sources.claim: 22.6 km / 18 min by road.

sources.title: French Tech Toulon — Meetups page
sources.claim: Monthly Tue-Thu meetups gathering tech, innovation and entrepreneurship enthusiasts; tech-weekend overlap requires Thu arrival.

sources.title: Info83 — Var Gaming Festival 2026
sources.claim: 30 January - 1 February 2026 at Hôtel départemental du Var, Toulon; 500+ visitors Saturday; 80-person Global Game Jam.

sources.title: ISEN Méditerranée — ActInSpace 2026
sources.claim: 30-31 January 2026, 24-hour space hackathon at ISEN Méditerranée Toulon; CNES, ESA, Thales Alenia Space, Airbus partners.

sources.title: Pôle Mer Méditerranée — Mer & Défense 2026
sources.claim: Journée Mer & Défense 11 June 2026, Palais Neptune Toulon; naval combat transformation, drones, autonomous maritime systems.
